subject: Temporary reserved lane for model-sensitivity sweep - autoscale exception request
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-11T09:42:00Z
Subject: Request: short-term reserved lane for Skyline model-sensitivity sweep

Hi team,

We have a timeboxed ask from Skyline AI: a model-sensitivity sweep for their enterprise pilot. They want a contiguous 72-hour window to run large-batch sweeps across ~300 model configs. Based on initial profiling, we should reserve 50 A100-equivalent GPU slots for the run to avoid long queue times and noisy neighbor interference.

Specifics:
- Window requested: Dec 20 00:00 UTC -> Dec 23 00:00 UTC (72 hours)
- Base reservation: 50 GPUs (A100 class)
- Autoscale exception ask: allow burst to 80 GPUs for up to 4 consecutive hours if queue backlog > 1k tokens/min for more than 15 minutes
- Models: mixture of 13B and 70B variants with quantized weights (mostly fp16/ggml-like)
- Business note: Skyline is testing throughput-to-cost tradeoffs for a potential dedicated contract (Deal DL-9831).

Attaching the sweep plan (model_sweep_plan.pdf) — includes estimated token volumes, per-job runtime, and priority tags. The customer prefers an uninterrupted run.

Can capacity/ops evaluate whether this can be scheduled without violating SLA for existing dedicated tenants? Also need guidance on how to bill the reservation vs. overage.

Thanks,
Marcus
Senior Product Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-11T12:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: short-term reserved lane for Skyline model-sensitivity sweep

Marcus — thanks for the details, this is helpful. A few quick questions before I loop security/finance:

1) Cost/commitment: will Skyline accept a billable short-term reservation (they indicated ‘pilot budget’) or do we need to treat this as a free courtesy? If billable, what's the expected amount (Ben, can you confirm)?
2) GPU family: you said A100-equivalent; please confirm exact instance type (A100 80GB, A100 40GB, or something else). That affects memory for the 70B runs and scheduling granularity.
3) Impact: confirm which other dedicated customers overlap in the same region/cluster and whether there are active canaries or rollouts during Dec 20-23. Marissa — can ops run a quick contention simulation?

If we decide to approve, I'll need a concise runbook and an exception approval (ops + infra lead) to temporarily relax autoscale caps for that pool. I've copied Dev to track any infra changes to the routing policy.

Please reply with answers by EOD Dec 13 — Skyline wants a firm start date by Dec 16 so they can finalize internal schedules.

— Irene
Director, Customer Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-11T14:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: short-term reserved lane for Skyline model-sensitivity sweep

Irene — we can make this billable under the DL-9831 pilot terms. Skyline confirmed they can allocate pilot budget to cover a short reservation. My estimate for 50 GPUs for 72 hours (A100-40 equivalent) plus potential 4-hour burst to 80 GPUs works out to approximately $32k in consumption (covers reserved pricing + overage allowance). I'll attach a quick reservation_draft.docx that we can use to confirm chargeable scope.

Note: If we charge, finance will need a signed SOW or PO that references DL-9831. I'll start the PO draft once we lock policy and ops approval.

— Ben
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-12T08:15:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: short-term reserved lane for Skyline model-sensitivity sweep

Thanks — ops notes/questions:

- Need exact GPU type. If 70B runs hit >40GB memory, we must schedule on A100-80 (reduces available slot count in the pool).
- Can we compress the run into a nightly window (e.g., Dec 20-22, 22:00-08:00) to lower interference with daytime tenants? That would still provide Skyline the throughput they need but minimizes business-hour impact.
- Alternative: preemptible pool + checkpointing. If Skyline can tolerate job restarts; we can offer a cheaper path that doesn't require a hard reservation.

I've attached a short ops_runbook.md that outlines the exception approval path and emergency fallback (auto-fail to preemptible + throttling). For approval we'll need: ops lead (me) + infra lead (Dev) sign-off, and a scoped outbound routing policy that sets burst window to 80 GPUs for the specified window.

I'll run a contention sim today against the proposed window and post results by EOD. If we see >15% SLA risk for any active dedicated customer, we'll need to push to nights-only or require a higher reservation.

— Marissa
Head of Capacity Ops

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Sarah Kim <sarah@skyline.ai>
Date: 2026-12-13T17:28:00Z
Subject: RE: Request: short-term reserved lane for Skyline model-sensitivity sweep

All — quick summary and decision request:

- Accepted approach: Billable short-term reservation for Skyline (Ben confirmed budget). Deal: DL-9831.
- Ops requirement: Run on A100-80 for the 70B configs; that reduces effective slot count.
- Scheduling compromise: Proposed nightly window to reduce daytime impact. Marcus, confirm whether Skyline can accept Dec 20-22 22:00-08:00 UTC (two nights) instead of a contiguous 72-hour daytime window; if not, they get the contiguous slot but subject to higher reservation pricing.
- Autoscale exception: approve burst ceiling to 80 GPUs for up to 4 hours during the approved window, subject to Marissa's contention sim. If sim shows >15% SLA exposure to a dedicated tenant, we revert to burst=65 GPUs.

Action items:
1) Marcus — confirm the night-window acceptability by EOD Dec 14 and confirm GPU-family target (A100-80 vs A100-40).
2) Marissa — post contention sim by EOD Dec 13 and flag any tenants impacted.
3) Ben — prepare PO/SOW referencing DL-9831 and the agreed reservation pricing once Marcus confirms window.
4) Dev — please prepare the temporary routing policy and autoscale override blueprint; don't deploy until final sign-off.

If all agree, I'll approve a scoped exception once we have (a) confirmation from Marcus, (b) Marissa's sim, and (c) Ben's PO draft.

Sarah — tagging you for visibility. If you want the contiguous run rather than nights-only, please confirm ASAP so we can finalize ops scheduling.

Thanks,
Irene
Director, Customer Infrastructure
Redwood Inference
